verdict.rationale: Codex documents letting a user add/remove local or remote MCP servers, inspect which tools are available before they're used, and choose approval modes for file edits/commands (codex-docs-16, codex-docs-17, codex-docs-20, codex-docs-21, codex-docs-26). This gives meaningful control over external tool access, but the evidence describes per-developer CLI/config control rather than a centrally enforced, org-wide policy an engineering-lead could impose across a team; RBAC (codex-docs-28) covers API/dashboard permissions, not agent tool-access restrictions specifically. missing for 10: org-level enforced allowlists/denylists for MCP or plugin access, admin dashboard for restricting integrations across a team, independent verification that restrictions can't be bypassed locally.
